column3: The Greek has plural “Sabbaths” and says He was teaching them; “began” and “the people” are supplied.
“What do You want with us” interprets the Greek idiom “what to us and to You.”
“The demon” and “the man” make the Greek pronoun referents explicit; “before them all” expands “into the midst.”
“Jesus” supplies the unnamed subject and pronoun referent; the Greek also describes Him rising from the synagogue.
“Began” is supplied before the Greek “was serving.”
The Greek makes those who had sick people the active bringers; BSB recasts this as sick people being brought and names Jesus for a pronoun.
“People” and the second “demons” make Greek referents explicit.
“Jesus” supplies the unnamed subject; “tried to keep” renders the Greek imperfect “were detaining.”
